results.title: Equality of the full final-answer law
results.target: Observation-law equivalence of the exact two parameter-matched Gaussian mechanisms
results.input_contract: XB=x+sqrt(v)ZB, XW=x+sqrt(kv)ZW; alpha=(k-1)/(k+1), beta=2/(k+1); TL=XB+sqrt(r_a)ZA and TP=alpha XB+beta XW+sqrt(r_a)ZA; Y=1{T>0}.
assumptions: v>0, k>1 and finite r_B,r_W>=0.
Member and output noises are independent standard normals, fresh across trials.
The complete stimulus/announcer design is fixed or has the same exogenous joint law in both mechanisms.
results.conclusion: Alpha+beta=1 and alpha^2+k beta^2=1 give the same N(x,v+r_a) final-score law and hence the same probit answer law. Independent repetitions give equal full score/answer vector laws conditional on the same complete design.
limitations: Equality is in law, not pathwise under a coupling.
Matching stimulus marginals alone is insufficient.
At k=1 the claimed two-input interpretation degenerates.
This exact pair does not represent every possible experiment or fit participant contributions.
results.operational_model: Matched one-input and two-input Gaussian mechanisms with fixed/exogenous common design
results.origin_status: PASS local deliverable seal and independent research verification
results.residual_scope: No actual member contribution or whole-model equivalence under other observations is inferred.

results.title: Equal answers with different model interventions
results.target: Different do(XW=w) response dependence in the equal-answer pair
results.input_contract: Same exact Gaussian pair; replace XW structurally by w and preserve other independent equations.
assumptions: v>0, k>1 and finite r_B,r_W>=0.
Member and output noises are independent standard normals, fresh across trials.
The complete stimulus/announcer design is fixed or has the same exogenous joint law in both mechanisms.
results.conclusion: Under L the intervention leaves the response law unchanged; under P the success probability Phi((alpha x+beta w)/sqrt(alpha^2 v+r_a)) is strictly increasing in w. Both positive-weight inputs are causally consequential in P.
limitations: The intervention is on the stipulated model, not evidence of a feasible human manipulation.
The result does not identify the mechanism used by an actual participant group.

results.title: Passive same-trial continuous and binary discrimination
results.target: Conditional dependence of the worse member’s passive signal and final answer
results.input_contract: Observe XW,Y or Q=1{XW>0},Y on the same trial at fixed x,a, without changing the mechanism.
assumptions: v>0, k>1 and finite r_B,r_W>=0.
Member and output noises are independent standard normals, fresh across trials.
The complete stimulus/announcer design is fixed or has the same exogenous joint law in both mechanisms.
The signal and final answer are linked by trial.
The observation is passive and conditioning is retained.
results.conclusion: Under L the private signal/bit and answer are independent. Under P Cov(XW,Y|x,a)=beta k v phi(x/sqrt(v+r_a))/sqrt(v+r_a)>0 and Cov(Q,Y|x,a)>0; all four binary-pair cells remain positive.
limitations: Pooled stimuli can induce association under L.
Unlinked marginals do not supply the discriminating dependence.
A finite observed cell never logically rules out either model.
results.operational_model: Matched one-input and two-input Gaussian mechanisms with fixed/exogenous common design
results.origin_status: PASS local deliverable seal and independent research verification
results.residual_scope: Passivity and trial linkage require independent justification in an empirical design.

results.title: Independent bit error and the separation boundary
results.target: Covariance and full recorded-pair law under independent Bernoulli bit flips
results.input_contract: Q prime=Q xor E with E Bernoulli(epsilon), independent of the scientific pair and freshly independent across trials.
assumptions: v>0, k>1 and finite r_B,r_W>=0.
Member and output noises are independent standard normals, fresh across trials.
The complete stimulus/announcer design is fixed or has the same exogenous joint law in both mechanisms.
Recording errors are independent, with the stated error rate.
results.conclusion: Cov(Q prime,Y)=(1-2 epsilon)Cov(Q,Y). Positive separation survives below one half, vanishes into equal recorded-pair sequence laws at one half, and can be direction-corrected by reversing bits above one half.
limitations: Dependent recording errors are outside the identity.
Equality at error one half concerns the stipulated recorded observations, not all potential observations.
results.operational_model: Matched one-input and two-input Gaussian mechanisms with fixed/exogenous common design
results.origin_status: PASS local deliverable seal and independent research verification
results.residual_scope: An actual recording channel’s independence and error rate remain empirical premises.

results.title: Fixed-sample error control and nonuniformity
results.target: Finite error bound with a known baseline and positive separation lower bound
results.input_contract: iid fixed-design recorded pairs; known p prime q and delta>=delta0>0; use mean Q prime Y threshold p prime q+delta0/2.
assumptions: v>0, k>1 and finite r_B,r_W>=0.
Member and output noises are independent standard normals, fresh across trials.
The complete stimulus/announcer design is fixed or has the same exogenous joint law in both mechanisms.
Baseline and separation lower bound are known and applicable.
Trials are independent repetitions.
results.conclusion: Each error is at most exp(-n delta0^2/2). Without a uniform positive gap, TV(P_n,L_n)<=2n delta and the error sum is at least 1-2n delta, so no fixed finite sample uniformly separates the full unseparated class. The exact illustration delta=1/6 gives threshold count 72 at n=216 and each error <=exp(-3).
limitations: The illustration is mathematical, not a collected dataset or executed study.
Error control is not finite certainty.
The known-gap guarantee cannot be transferred to unknown arbitrarily small alternatives.
results.operational_model: Matched one-input and two-input Gaussian mechanisms with fixed/exogenous common design
results.origin_status: PASS local deliverable seal and independent research verification
results.residual_scope: Unknown marginals and numerical implementation require a different rule and separate qualification.

results.title: One-sided sequential detection with unknown marginals
results.target: False-ever-selection control and pointwise finite detection of positive binary dependence
results.input_contract: iid binary pairs; empirical c_n=b_n-p_n q_n; epsilon_n=sqrt(log(6n(n+1)/gamma)/(2n)); stop only for c_n>3 epsilon_n.
assumptions: 0<gamma<1.
The null is independence and each alternative has fixed positive covariance.
The rule is interpreted in exact real arithmetic.
results.conclusion: The probability of ever falsely selecting the dependent alternative under the null is at most gamma, while every fixed positive alternative is detected in finite time almost surely.
limitations: The rule returns no null answer and has no uniform finite stopping-time guarantee.
No verified floating-point classifier is supplied.
Conservative numerical errors and thresholds must still vanish for the eventual-detection argument.
results.origin_status: PASS local deliverable seal and independent research verification
results.residual_scope: A total two-answer service is not obtained.

results.title: No uniformly reliable terminating null branch without separation
results.target: Incompatibility of null almost-sure termination with uniform two-answer errors over near-null alternatives
results.input_contract: Fixed uniform independent-pair null at x=0,v=1,k=3,r_a=0 and alternatives delta=(1-2 epsilon)/6 decreasing to zero.
assumptions: The procedure is nonanticipating.
It terminates almost surely under the fixed null.
Uniform null and alternative error bounds sum to less than one.
results.conclusion: No such two-answer procedure exists over the full near-null alternative class: finite stopping prefixes can be approximated by alternatives closely enough to retain the null decision probability.
limitations: The theorem does not require alternative-side almost-sure termination or finite expected stopping time.
Separated subclasses can admit stronger services.
It is an exact model result, not a general impossibility of all empirical science.
results.operational_model: Sequential binary-pair laws with a fixed null and arbitrarily close alternatives
results.origin_status: PASS local deliverable seal and independent research verification
results.residual_scope: Null nontermination remains an explicit service boundary, not a hidden completed answer.

results.title: Official-input reanalysis of the 15-dyad comparison
results.target: Hash-pinned aggregate reproduction and numerical agreement for the same published 15 dyads
results.input_contract: Two official objects declared by INPUTS.json; archive and workbook SHA-256 checked before parsing, then selected MAT hash, shapes, columns and workbook ranges checked.
assumptions: Use the exact official decisions ZIP and Experiment 2 workbook.
Python 3.12 and exact declared numpy/scipy/pandas/openpyxl pins.
Pairing unit is dyad, contrast is INF minus IND, all response trials are retained despite timing missingness.
results.conclusion: The fresh source-prescribed run passed all 13 original synthetic tests, reconstructed the 15-dyad official-input comparison, reconciled all 120 workbook sensitivity estimates to four decimals with both separately written numerical cores, preserved the one negative slope, and reproduced the original aggregate bytes. The mean INF-minus-IND difference is 0.7126365005104668, t(14)=2.704264596388044, p=0.01711311760610826, 95% interval [0.14743541713250896,1.2778375838884246]. The checked cross-implementation maximum difference is 3.0215846713588235e-08. A separate corrupt-input subprocess completed with intended exit 2.
limitations: This is reanalysis of the same observations, not a new participant experiment or replication.
The INF condition lacks private responses, so member contribution is not identified.
Announcer role does not isolate contribution.
Graphical panels and original author-code execution are not newly verified.
Record-level data never enters the public projection.

results.origin_status: PASS local deliverable seal and independent research verification
results.residual_scope: FINITE_ONLY same-data numerical reproduction. Original observations are not a new sample; actual-member contribution, graphical panels, experimental replication and specialist validation remain outside the evidenced scope.
